catalog_locator: §3.3 Tones, printed p. 4 = PDF page 6 of 34 (page rendered and read as an image during this reading)
catalog_quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Ninkyop is complex due to morphophonemic alternations. The underlying system has three tone heights, e.g. zíg row of ridges / zig knife / zìŋ giving gift. There is also a rising tone; yǔŋ love / ᶆwǐ ground / ɣwǒm old person and a falling tone; ᶆwârr joy / nʒôrɲ horn / ngû feather. The falling tone is much rarer than the rising tone. A low-mid tone that occurs only in words of two syllables or more. Examples; ǹjɔ᷅r evening / nshi᷅d tick / nyúŋʒyɛ᷅ animal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ninkyop (Kaninkon) is described as a tone language with three underlying level tone heights (high, mid, low) plus rising, falling and a low-mid contour; tone is lexically contrastive on monosyllables (zíg / zig / zìŋ) and raised as a plural-marking process. The source says nothing at all about word stress or accent, so no stress placement can be read from it.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated regarding stress; the tone description notes that the falling tone is rare and the low-mid tone occurs only in words of two or more syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone illustrated on citation-form nouns and verbs (mostly monosyllabic roots); the source is an annotated wordlist based on three days of fieldwork (2005) and the unpublished Kadima & Jerzyk phonology; draft 'not for citation without reference to the authors'.
new_statements.identity_note: The one opened description (Blench & Kadima 2011) covers Ninkyop = Ninkyob = Kaningkom/Kaninkon/Kaninkwom, i.e. the Kaningdom dialect kani1278 of kani1277 (villages Bakin Kogi, Gerti, Amere; Turan / Mbeco / Nkpa Nkun pronunciations), not Nindem (nind1241), for which no description of any kind was found. The two Ilorin theses (Kaninkon / Kaningkon) also concern the Ninkyob side.
